title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (October 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, re-read this session off conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-10-26 is the last Tuesday of October 2027. CORROBORATED FOR OCTOBER SPECIFICALLY, 3 of 3 and every one double-sourced, from editions this session fetched direct 2026-09-06 and verified against their own "Source: October <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" lines rather than trusted by slug: CCI-Oct-2022 (887,350 bytes, Updated 2022-10-25), CCI-Oct-2023 (1,247,171 bytes, Updated 2023-10-31), CCI-Oct-2024 (894,379 bytes, Updated 2024-10-29). Each is the last Tuesday of its October, and each was ANNOUNCED IN ADVANCE by its own September predecessor's next-release line, also re-read this session: CCI-Sept-2022 "The next release is Tuesday, October 25", CCI-Sept-2023 "Tuesday, October 31", CCI-Sep-2024 "Tuesday, October 29th". October 2023 is the chain's most useful case, because 2023-10-31 is the FIFTH Tuesday of its month -- the rule is "last Tuesday", not "fourth Tuesday", and this is the sourced instance that distinguishes them. INDEPENDENTLY DATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER: fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-06) posts a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table whose tenth row reads "Tuesday, October 26 | Monthly Index | August 2027" -- one of twelve 2027 rows, all twelve matching this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays. That corroborates the calendar arithmetic, not the Conference Board's intentions. No October-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified October record. notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-09-28 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain. Proposed rather than skipped because October is the venue for two things this session could not settle, not because the chain should keep rolling. FIRST, IT IS THE COLLIDING MIRROR OF THIS SESSION'S OWN NULL. 2027-10-26 is FOMC day one (the meeting is Oct 26-27), so it joins Jan 26, Apr 27 and Jul 27 as one of 2027's four collision prints -- and the 08-31 sibling's July-vs-August null plus this session's September-vs-July null now make TWO independent clean-vs-colliding comparisons that both came back 0 of 9. A third is worth having, and October is the only 2027 month that supplies it against a Q4 backdrop. SECOND, IT SCORES THIS SESSION'S THRESHOLD-BAND FINDING. This ledger measured all ten first-print-to-restatement pairs the chain can source and found the flips are not random: a first-printed Expectations reading within 2.0 points of 80.0 flipped side on revision 3 of 5 times, and one further away 0 of 5. The October edition restates September 2027, so it is the document that tests the band rather than argues it. THREE CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS. (1) October's cut-off lags are 6 / 7 / 6 days (2022-10-19, 2023-10-24, 2024-10-23 against their releases) -- SHORTER than September's 7/8/7 and much shorter than August's 7/9/6, so do not borrow a neighbour's; project 10-19 to 10-20 for 2027. (2) The October print is a collision print, and its panel therefore CANNOT hear its own month's decision -- the opposite configuration to September's, which is the cleanest within-quarter contrast this chain has ever had available. (3) Do not re-fetch the publisher concurrently: this session tripped its origin's captcha (HTTP 200 serving a 1,021-byte "User validation required" page, error code 421) by issuing parallel requests, and a byte-count check is the only thing that catches it.
